static_traits.name: Wang Ping
static_traits.family_status: No children, Not mentioned other family members
static_traits.social_status: Generally Good relationships with colleagues; has one close friend but has not yet discussed Self-doubt with them; confidence affected by Self-doubt in Social situations
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; no prior psychological counseling or treatment history; no similar psychological problems before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, highly cooperative, Neutral attitude; able to identify and describe automatic thoughts and emotions; tends toward Self-denial when praised

basic_info.main_problem: I feel my parents' praise for my interactions with children has no value, because anyone could do it. This way of thinking has led to feelings of inadequacy and Self-doubt.
basic_info.core_demands: I seek counseling because these Self-doubts have started affecting my confidence at Work and overall well-being; I hope to change how I feel about myself.
growth_experiences: Self-doubt and feelings of inadequacy appeared about two years ago after becoming a Children's librarian; stress was moderate at the time, worrying about failing to meet others' expectations; the problem then developed into persistently negating positive feedback and focusing only on one's own shortcomings; these thoughts mostly arise in Work scenarios interacting with children and their parents; tried self-challenging but has not yet been able to change.

core_beliefs: My efforts are not particularly special, anyone could do them

special_situations.event: After helping the child complete reading homework, the parent expresses thanks/praise face to face
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others praise me, it is usually just out of politeness, not because I really did well
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Immediately negating praise, lowering self-evaluation, and reducing interaction with others that day
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are just being polite, it is not that I did well; I am not particularly special

special_situations.event: In daily interactions with children and parents and in work evaluation situations
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only by continuously proving oneself, meeting or even exceeding expectations, does one count as qualified; otherwise one is not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly pressuring and proving oneself, repeatedly finding fault afterward
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: No matter what I do, it is not good enough

special_situations.event: Frequently receives positive feedback or thanks from parents
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my Work is something others can easily do, then this praise is meaningless
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Devalues one's own contributions and refuses to internalize positive feedback into self-evaluation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Anyone could do it, I have no real value

special_situations.event: Thinking about expressing one's Self-doubt and vulnerability to a close friend
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If these feelings are discussed, one will be seen as weak or incompetent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids discussing such topics with friends, stays silent
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will appear weak, unworthy of discussing this with others

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be genuinely recognized, seen, and affirmed for her professional value
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being seen as weak or incompetent, worrying that others' praise is insincere and will ultimately be negated
defense_goal: Lowering expectations and the risk of being negated by negating positive feedback
Avoiding expressing vulnerability to avoid being looked down upon
Continuously proving oneself to gain a sense of safety

object_relations.self_representation: A not-good-enough professional who needs to keep proving oneself
object_relations.object_representation: A judge who is polite on the surface but picky and insincere inside (such as parents)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When parents express thanks or praise for her work
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Subconsciously interprets praise as politeness rather than genuine recognition, worried that they have 'deceived' the other
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Downplaying praise in a calm but firm tone, emphasizing 'it is just politeness', quickly shifting the topic, avoiding lingering on discussions of self-worth

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When thinking about discussing Self-doubt and vulnerability with a close friend
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing that expressing vulnerability will be seen as weakness and unworthiness, being looked down upon by others
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Choosing not to disclose these feelings, turning to neutral topics instead, keeping a restrained tone and answering self-evaluation questions briefly

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: At work, faces frequent interaction with children and parents where performance needs to be evaluated
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Seeing others' expectations as a high threat, believing that the slightest inadequacy will lead to being negated
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Displaying excessive diligence and perfect standards, emphasizing the need to work harder, masking insecurity with statements like 'I still need to improve'

manifestations: Questions the value of parents' praise, believing 'anyone can do it', and doubts whether they truly made an impact
At work, hard to integrate positive feedback into one's self-image
outcomes: Self-doubt and feelings of inadequacy intensify
Declining motivation and interest, affecting self-care

manifestations: Having a close friend but not yet sharing Self-doubt due to embarrassment and fear of appearing weak
After being praised, tends to reduce interaction with others

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Being overly self-critical in Work scenarios, emphasizing 'No matter what I do, it is not good enough'
Quickly finding shortcomings after receiving praise, focusing only on the negative

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Worrying about failing to meet others' expectations, making 'must prove oneself' a self-Demand
Measures self-worth by others' potential standards

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Interpreting parents' praise as 'just politeness', assuming the other party is insincere
Worries about being seen as weak, presumes others will look down on him

positive_force: Parents frequently give positive feedback, showing their interaction with children has real effects
Good relationships with colleagues, with some Social support foundation
Willing to seek professional help and willing to try changing
Having a strong educational background and professional competence (Master's degree in library science)
negative_force: Deeply ingrained cognitive patterns of negating positive thinking and mental filtering
Overly cares about others' expectations, relies on external evaluation, self-worth is hard to internalize
Avoids seeking support for fear of seeming weak
Persistent self-pressure and self-criticism, affecting self-care and work confidence

target_behavior.behavior: Automatically negating praise or positive feedback and developing Anxiety and Self-doubt, then reducing interaction with others
antecedent: Interacts with children and parents and receives praise/thanks
When one's performance or contribution is mentioned in work situations
target_behavior.core_reason: Stemming from long-term Self-doubt and the core belief 'I am not good enough', plus the automatic thought of interpreting praise as politeness
target_behavior.function: Avoiding the risk of potential negation or exposure of inadequacy, maintaining a sense of control over self-evaluation
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased self-confidence at Work, performance affected, Reduced social interaction that day, overall well-being and self-care damaged
